task.description: PR #4629 fixed the __pycache__ self-rejection half of the governed-promotion bug, but the second, separately-flagged failure mode is still open: `git revert`... err, `promote_supervisor_runtime.py`s _assert_relative_identity/_open_relative_descriptor raises ValueError("Candidate Git directory is a symlink or has the wrong type: [Errno 20] Not a directory: '.git'") when verifying a freshly-materialized candidate at command-runtimes/<sha>, even though `ls -la`/`file` confirm .git really is a plain directory (a standalone clone, not a worktree gitlink file or symlink). Reproduced 2026-08-08 running `bash scripts/sync-dev-root.sh` against a clean candidate for commit 619acd04184e8d3fc3aef322d160e7c9106670ad (evidence: /home/lupin/pantheon-ci-deploy/runtime/promotion-evidence/supervisor-runtime-promotion-20260808T143911364247Z-100873.json). The check uses os.open(name, O_RDONLY|O_DIRECTORY|O_NOFOLLOW|O_CLOEXEC, dir_fd=parent_descriptor) inside _open_relative_descriptor (scripts/promote_supervisor_runtime.py ~line 738), called via _assert_relative_identity(handle.descriptor, ".git", handle.git_identity, label="Candidate Git directory", require_directory=True) around line 1065. ENOTDIR from an O_DIRECTORY open of a real directory usually means the dir_fd (handle.descriptor, supposed to be the candidate root) is not actually pointing at a directory by the time this runs -- worth checking how/where `handle.descriptor` and `handle.git_identity` get captured earlier in build_candidate_runtime_identity / _open_candidate_root_handle for a stale-descriptor or wrong-fd bug, rather than assuming .git itself is malformed. This blocks ALL governed supervisor promotions (sync-dev-root.sh dies with FATAL after this), forcing manual workarounds (direct git checkout + supervisor_watchdog --record-intent + SIGTERM) that skip the immutable-candidate safety guarantees entirely.
